subject.title: chore(deps): bump the actions group across 1 directory with 14 updates

question: Should OpenClaw accept these 14 grouped executable-action upgrades in secret-bearing and release-critical workflows after an exact-head refresh and targeted validation?
rationale: Automated review can verify pin shape and input compatibility, but only a maintainer can accept the upstream supply-chain and operational boundary for actions that receive credentials or publish artifacts.

options.title: Approve after exact-head validation
options.body: Keep the grouped update, refresh it onto current main, verify tag-to-SHA provenance, and require the sensitive workflow checks to pass before merge.

options.title: Split sensitive action upgrades
options.body: Separate Codex, token-minting, registry, Docker publishing, and CodeQL changes from lower-risk setup and housekeeping actions for narrower review and rollback.

options.title: Defer the grouped bump
options.body: Leave the current pins in place until the upstream changes or failing checks can be reviewed with higher confidence.

recommendation.title: Approve after exact-head validation
recommendation.body: Keep the grouped update, refresh it onto current main, verify tag-to-SHA provenance, and require the sensitive workflow checks to pass before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent history most strongly connects this account to CI stabilization, release publishing, and Docker workflow safeguards spanning the highest-risk changed surfaces.
